finding.claim: GET /rss passes the attacker-supplied `u` parameter straight into URI.open, which fetches arbitrary http/https URLs server-side and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller.

trace.note: `params[:u]` is passed to `URI.open` with no transformation.
open-uri issues the request from the server, follows HTTP redirects by default, and reads the body.
`data[0, 400]` returns the first 400 bytes to the requester, so the response is readable (not blind).

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. No scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no IP/private-range or link-local block (169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, RFC1918), no port restriction, and no redirect validation. The 400-byte truncation limits how much is returned but does not restrict what is requested.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check is at app.rb:14, but it sits in the separate /trusted route (lines 12-16), not on the /rss path. The /rss handler (app.rb:7-10) has no scheme, host, IP, or port restriction before URI.open at app.rb:8.
verdict.reason: params[:u] at app.rb:8 is attacker-controlled from the query string and goes straight into URI.open(...).read with no validation, and data[0, 400] at app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched response to the caller, so the SSRF is readable. The trace lines all match the code. One minor imprecision: open-uri also accepts ftp:// URLs, not only http/https, which does not change the verdict.
